questions.stem: Musts, the budget and overrides get rule literals; access windows and crews' time off do not. Why?

options.text: CP-SAT offers no way to put a window behind a literal
options.says: The design note says a window could get a literal if it were negotiable.

options.text: They cannot take part in a clash, so naming them is moot
options.says: A pin outside a window is a clash the model must find.

options.text: They are physical facts the planner cannot act on
options.says: Right: an explanation is useful only if the reader can act on every rule it names.

options.text: check_overrides tests them as data before the solve
options.says: check_overrides checks overrides as data: unknown circuits, crews, kinds and weeks.

origin.section: An Override Is One More Rule, and Every Rule a Planner Can Change Sits Behind a Literal

questions.stem: Two pins clash on crew K1 in a season that also has two musts and a budget. Which rules does the explanation list?

options.text: Only the two pins, since the other rules are no part of it
options.says: Right: the other three are not mentioned, because they are not part of the clash.

options.text: All five rules, since the whole season has no plan at all
options.says: The explanation lists a minimal set: the two pins.

options.text: The two pins and the budget, which every plan must keep
options.says: The budget is not part of this clash and is not listed.

options.text: The two musts, since they were set before the planner's pins
options.says: The musts are not part of this clash and are not listed.

origin.section: Overrides Have a Price, and a Clash Names Its Rules

questions.stem: The overlapping-pins test also forces circuit C, which fits. Why is that override in the test?

options.text: So the budget becomes part of the conflict the test expects
options.says: The expected explanation names only the two pins.

options.text: So the test can check that C is trimmed before the pins
options.says: The test expects INFEASIBLE, with no trims to check.

options.text: So circuit C pushes both pinned trims past the season's end
options.says: C takes one week; the test needs a rule the explanation leaves out.

options.text: So an explanation that lists every override fails the test
options.says: Right: override 1 is a rule the explanation must leave out.

origin.section: Six Tests: Three Overrides, Two Clashes, One Data Check
